label: else_if_chain
graph_version: 3.9.8 (3.9.7 + one primary per misconception (S9c) and the four remaining sibling edges (S9b), 2026-11-04; listed in revision_3_9_8)

edges.label:
[0] everyday_reading (E): Folk meaning: a list of rules 'if A ...; else if B ...' reads like a set of independent rules where every one that applies is followed, in any order. In Java the conditions are tested top to bottom and only the first true branch runs.
[1] misconception (M) -> ElsIf: wrong rule: Java has an elsif keyword for multi-way branches. Right rule: Multi-way branches are written else if.
[2] misconception (M) -> MultipleElseIfBranchesRun: wrong rule: Every true branch of an else-if chain runs. Right rule: Only the first branch whose condition is true runs.
[3] misconception (M) -> ElseIfChainExitsEarly: wrong rule: An else-if chain can finish before it has tested all its conditions, even when no branch has run. Right rule: The conditions of an else-if chain are tested in order until one is true; only then, or after the last test (and the final else), does the chain end.
[4] misconception (M) -> ElseIfOrderIgnored: wrong rule: The conditions of an else-if chain can be tested in any order (e.g. the matching or most specific one first). Right rule: The conditions are tested top to bottom and the first true one wins, so their order changes the result when conditions overlap.
[5] inconsistent_trace (T) -> ElsIf: Applies the chain rule (LT) unevenly: stops at the first true condition on some inputs but continues testing (and running branches) on others. (here mixing in: "Java has an elsif keyword for multi-way branches")

[0] names_the_element (N): An else-if chain (multiway if-else) is a sequence of if-else statements in which each else is another if, choosing among mutually exclusive possibilities.
[1] states_the_rule (S): Written if (c1) S1 else if (c2) S2 ... else Sn; the ifs are nested to test from among a number of mutually exclusive possibilities, and the final else needs no condition.

[0] line_by_line_trace (LT): Test c1; if true run S1 and leave the chain; otherwise test c2, and so on; if no condition is true, run the final else (if any); then continue after the chain.
[1] output_prediction (OP): Exactly one branch (or none, without a final else) runs: in the tax example an income of 100000 gives rate .25, because income < 47450 is false and income < 114650 is the first true test.
[2] one_step_execution (OS): One execution evaluates conditions in order until the first true one, applies that branch's changes, and skips all later tests.

[0] relation_to_neighbour (R): An else-if chain is an if-else whose else part is another if-else, so every rule of if-else (one test, one branch) applies at each link.
[1] purpose_of_the_whole (P): Plan: multiway selection / classification into ranges - pick one category for a value (tax bracket, sign of x, grade).

[0] predict_a_change (C) -> ElsIf: Reordering the tests preserves behaviour only if the conditions are mutually exclusive; with overlapping, ordered thresholds (income < 47450, < 114650 ...) swapping two tests changes the result. Replacing else if by separate ifs makes several branches run.
[1] transfer_to_a_new_program (X): Use an else-if chain when exactly one of several mutually exclusive, ordered conditions applies; use separate ifs when several actions may apply, and a switch when testing one expression against many fixed values.
[2] diagnose_an_error (D): rule broken: Java has no elsif/elif keyword; the chain is written else if. Kind: compile-time. Trigger class: Writing elsif (c) or elif (c): the compiler reports a missing semicolon or unknown symbol.
[3] diagnose_an_error (D): rule broken: The first true condition wins, so a broader test placed earlier hides later ones. Kind: silent logic error. Trigger class: if (x < 100) ... else if (x < 10) ...: the second branch is unreachable for every input; no compiler error.
wrong: Java has an elsif keyword for multi-way branches. | right: Multi-way branches are written else if.

wrong: An else-if chain can finish before it has tested all its conditions, even when no branch has run. | right: The conditions of an else-if chain are tested in order until one is true; only then, or after the last test (and the final else), does the chain end.

wrong: The conditions of an else-if chain can be tested in any order (e.g. the matching or most specific one first). | right: The conditions are tested top to bottom and the first true one wins, so their order changes the result when conditions overlap.
wrong: Every true branch of an else-if chain runs. | right: Only the first branch whose condition is true runs.
wrong: Every true branch of an else-if chain runs. | right: Only the first branch whose condition is true runs.

Both pick one of several alternatives. A switch compares one value with constant case labels and falls through without break; an else-if chain tests each condition in turn and runs only the first true branch.
An else-if chain is an if-else whose else part is another if.
